# Config key reference

HOW TO RUN: `python -m stt config-docs` writes this file again from the code (add `--out FILE` for another place). Never edit it by hand: a test fails when it is out of date.
Use a key in a config file as `section:` / `key:` (nested keys are nested blocks), or on the command line as `--set section.key=value` (lists and dicts as JSON).

Status column: the tag at the start of the key's description in the code (`DEFAULT` = a starting value you may change, `NEW` = added after the original brief, `REQUIRED` = no default, you must set it). A key without a tag shows `DEFAULT` or `REQUIRED` from its default value. The code carries no `LOCKED` mark: the locked choices are in docs/DECISIONS.md and docs/PRD.md.

<a id="section-runtime"></a>
## `runtime`

The `runtime` section, defined by the Config component. Keys: `online` (explicit switch for running at home; the pipeline is offline by default), `seed` (applied everywhere for determinism) and `device` (where the model computes).

| Key | Type | Default | Status | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `runtime.online` | bool | false | DEFAULT | True only at home: allows online mode. Offline by default. |
| `runtime.seed` | int | 42 | DEFAULT | DEFAULT 42. Seed applied everywhere for deterministic runs. |
| `runtime.device` | 'cpu' \| 'cuda' \| 'auto' | "cpu" | DEFAULT | DEFAULT cpu (the behaviour before this key existed). cuda: train and score on the GPU; the run FAILS with exit code 2 if no usable GPU is found (never a silent fall back to the CPU). auto: cuda when torch reports a usable GPU, otherwise cpu (the choice is logged at INFO). Environment: STT__RUNTIME__DEVICE. |

<a id="section-data"></a>
## `data`

The `data` section.

| Key | Type | Default | Status | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `data.source.type` | str | (required) | REQUIRED | Source name in the DataSource registry: `csv` or `hf_parquet`. |
| `data.source.path` | Path | (required) | REQUIRED | Folder with the data (a folder with manifest.csv, or a folder of parquet files). |
| `data.columns.id` | str \| None | null | DEFAULT | Optional column with a unique sample id. Without it the audio path is the id. |
| `data.columns.audio` | str | (required) | REQUIRED | Column with the audio file path (parquet: the audio struct). |
| `data.columns.text` | str | (required) | REQUIRED | Column with the transcript. |
| `data.columns.group` | str \| None | null | DEFAULT | Column with the group (for example the lesson) that must not be split. |
| `data.columns.split` | str \| None | null | DEFAULT | Optional column with the source split name. |
| `data.group_fallback` | 'parent_dir' \| 'file_stem' \| 'fail' | "fail" | DEFAULT | DEFAULT fail. What to do without a group column; a wrong group causes train/test leakage. |
| `data.extra_types` | dict[str, 'str' \| 'int' \| 'float' \| 'bool'] | {} | DEFAULT | Column -> type of the values kept in `extra`; unlisted columns stay text. |
| `data.extract.dir` | Path \| None | null | DEFAULT | Folder for the extracted audio and manifest.csv (outside src/ and tests/). |
| `data.extract.overwrite` | bool | false | DEFAULT | DEFAULT false: reuse a complete earlier extraction. |
| `data.on_invalid` | 'skip' \| 'fail' | "skip" | DEFAULT | DEFAULT skip. `fail` stops at the first rejected sample. |
| `data.max_rejected_ratio` | float | 0.05 | DEFAULT | DEFAULT 0.05. The run fails when more than this fraction is rejected. |

<a id="section-split"></a>
## `split`

The `split` section.

| Key | Type | Default | Status | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `split.mode` | str | "grouped_ratio" | DEFAULT | DEFAULT grouped_ratio. Splitter in the registry: predefined, grouped_ratio, hash_group, time_block. |
| `split.group_key.column` | str \| None | null | DEFAULT | DEFAULT none = the DataSource group (`group_id`). Else a field name: group_id, id, source_split, or a key of `extra` (for example meta_source). |
| `split.group_key.regex` | str \| None | null | DEFAULT | DEFAULT none. A regular expression applied to the column value; its first capture group is the group. |
| `split.names` | tuple[str, Ellipsis] | ["train", "val", "test"] | DEFAULT | DEFAULT train, val, test. The split names, in order. |
| `split.ratios` | tuple[float, Ellipsis] | [0.8, 0.1, 0.1] | DEFAULT | DEFAULT 0.8, 0.1, 0.1. Must sum to 1, one per name. |
| `split.ratio_unit` | 'duration' \| 'samples' | "duration" | DEFAULT | DEFAULT duration. What the ratios measure. |
| `split.ratio_tolerance` | float | 0.05 | DEFAULT | DEFAULT 0.05 absolute. Allowed deviation from a requested ratio. |
| `split.seed` | int \| None | null | DEFAULT | DEFAULT none = use runtime.seed. |
| `split.min_samples_per_split` | int | 30 | DEFAULT | DEFAULT 30. Review when the data volume is known (O22). |
| `split.min_groups_per_split` | int | 2 | DEFAULT | DEFAULT 2. Review when the data volume is known (O22). |
| `split.on_oversized_group` | 'fail' \| 'warn' | "fail" | DEFAULT | DEFAULT fail. A group larger than a split can hold. |
| `split.on_overlap` | 'fail' \| 'drop_from_train' | "fail" | DEFAULT | DEFAULT fail. For `predefined`: a group present in several source splits. |
| `split.time_block.order_column` | str | "meta_seek" | DEFAULT | DEFAULT meta_seek. Key of `extra` with the start time (seconds) of the clip in its recording. |
| `split.time_block.guard_gap_sec` | float | 30.0 | DEFAULT | DEFAULT 30. Clips closer than this to the previous block are dropped. |
| `split.predefined.source_map` | dict[str, str] | {} | DEFAULT | DEFAULT empty = the source split name is the split name. Maps a source split name to a split name (for example eval: test). |
| `split.speaker_column` | str \| None | null | DEFAULT | DEFAULT none. Key of `extra` with the speaker or creator; the report then counts speakers shared between splits. |
| `split.dir` | Path \| None | null | DEFAULT | DEFAULT none = nothing is saved. Folder for saved splits (`<dir>/<version>/split.json`). |
| `split.version` | str | "v1" | DEFAULT | DEFAULT v1. A new version is the only way to create a new split. |
| `split.reuse` | bool | true | DEFAULT | DEFAULT true. Reuse a saved split of this version. |
| `split.export_csv` | bool | false | DEFAULT | DEFAULT false. Also write `split.csv` (id, split) next to split.json. |

<a id="section-subsample"></a>
## `subsample`

The `subsample` section.

| Key | Type | Default | Status | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `subsample.enabled` | bool | false | DEFAULT | DEFAULT false. Off: the splits are returned unchanged (the main runs use all the data). |
| `subsample.size.minutes` | float \| None | null | DEFAULT | Minutes of audio (the owner's unit). |
| `subsample.size.samples` | int \| None | null | DEFAULT | A number of samples. |
| `subsample.size.fraction` | float \| None | null | DEFAULT | A fraction (0 to 1] of the minutes of audio, for example 0.1 for one tenth. |
| `subsample.strategy` | str | "by_sample" | DEFAULT | DEFAULT by_sample. The unit of selection: by_sample or by_group (registry). |
| `subsample.scope` | 'train_only' \| 'all_splits' | "train_only" | DEFAULT | DEFAULT train_only. all_splits reduces Train, Val and Test by the same fraction (rehearsal only). |
| `subsample.val` | 'fixed' \| 'follow' | "fixed" | DEFAULT | DEFAULT fixed. follow reduces Val by the same share as Train (train_only scope). |
| `subsample.val_samples` | int \| None | null | NEW | NEW, DEFAULT none. A FIXED number of Val samples (a Val slice, for example 100), whatever the Train size. Train_only scope; not with val: follow. |
| `subsample.repeats` | int | 1 | DEFAULT | DEFAULT 1. How many draws of the same size the caller makes (repeat_index 0 to repeats-1). |
| `subsample.repeat_index` | int | 0 | NEW | NEW, DEFAULT 0. Which draw this run uses; must be below `repeats`. |
| `subsample.min_train_samples` | int | 10 | DEFAULT | DEFAULT 10. Fewer selected Train samples FAIL the run. |
| `subsample.preset` | str \| None | null | NEW | NEW, DEFAULT none. Name of a preset (smoke, tiny, work_like, half, full, or one of `presets`): it replaces size and, where defined, strategy and scope. |
| `subsample.presets` | dict[str, PresetConfig] | {} | DEFAULT | DEFAULT empty. Your own presets; the built-in ones are in the code (smoke, tiny, work_like, half, full). |
| `subsample.dir` | Path \| None | null | NEW | NEW, DEFAULT none = nothing is saved. Folder for the stored subsets (JSON, one file per spec). |

| Key | Type | Default | Status | Description |

| `text.train.timestamps` | str | "strip" | DEFAULT | DEFAULT strip. `keep` is not implemented in v1 (O3, O48). |
| `text.bracket.pairs` | tuple[tuple[str, str], Ellipsis] | [["[", "]"], ["(", ")"]] | DEFAULT | DEFAULT [] and (). Pairs of opening and closing characters. |
| `text.bracket.mode` | 'chars_only' \| 'with_content' \| 'keep' | "chars_only" | DEFAULT | DEFAULT chars_only (O25): remove the bracket characters, keep the content. |
| `text.punctuation.chars` | str | ".,;:!?…\"'“”‘’׳״־-–—" | DEFAULT | DEFAULT a standard Hebrew and Latin set. Every listed character is removed. |

| `text.quotes.map` | dict[str, str] | {"'": "׳", "’": "׳", "\"": "״", "“": "״", "”": "״"} | DEFAULT | DEFAULT: ' and the right single quote become geresh; ", curly double quotes become gershayim. |
| `text.unicode.invisible_chars` | str | "​‌‍‎‏‪‫‬‭‮⁠⁦⁧⁨⁩­﻿؜" | DEFAULT | DEFAULT zero-width, direction-control and similar characters, removed. |
| `text.timestamp_pattern` | str | "<\\\|(\\d+(?:\\.\\d+)?)\\\|>" | DEFAULT | DEFAULT Whisper-style <\|12.34\|>. A regular expression with ONE capture group holding the time in seconds. |
| `text.inventory.top_n` | int | 50 | DEFAULT | DEFAULT 50. How many characters (most frequent first) the report lists. |

<a id="section-features"></a>
## `features`

The `features` section.

| Key | Type | Default | Status | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `features.num_workers` | int | 0 | DEFAULT | DEFAULT 0 (O2). Threads used to fill the cache; 0 = one at a time. |
| `features.cache.enabled` | bool | false | DEFAULT | DEFAULT false. When true, features are computed once and stored as files. |
| `features.cache.dir` | Path \| None | null | DEFAULT | Folder of the cache (required when enabled; outside src/ and tests/). |
| `features.encoder_cache.enabled` | bool | false | DEFAULT | DEFAULT false (nothing changes). When true, the output of the frozen audio encoder is computed once per clip and reused for training, the Val loss and the decoding (identical results, about 8 times faster training, 3 times faster decoding on the CPU). |
| `features.encoder_cache.dir` | Path \| None | null | DEFAULT | Folder of the encoder cache (required when enabled; about 7.7 MB per clip for the turbo model in float32, half in float16). |
| `features.encoder_cache.dtype` | 'float16' \| 'float32' | "float16" | DEFAULT | DEFAULT float16 (half the disk; the self-check and the 8-clip test showed identical decoded text). float32 is exact. |
| `features.max_dropped_ratio` | float | 0.05 | DEFAULT | DEFAULT 0.05. The run fails when more than this fraction of labels is removed for length. |
| `features.downmix` | 'mean' | "mean" | DEFAULT | DEFAULT mean. Stereo is averaged to mono. |
| `features.shuffle` | bool | false | DEFAULT | DEFAULT false. When true the examples are put in a seeded random order. |
| `features.seed` | int \| None | null | DEFAULT | DEFAULT none = use runtime.seed. Seed of the shuffle. |

<a id="section-train"></a>
## `train`

The `train` section.

| Key | Type | Default | Status | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `train.freeze_policy` | str | "none" | DEFAULT | DEFAULT none (full fine-tuning). Registered: none, freeze_encoder. |
| `train.hyperparams.learning_rate` | float | 1e-05 | DEFAULT | DEFAULT 1e-5 (brief). Peak learning rate. |
| `train.hyperparams.max_steps` | int | 100 | DEFAULT | DEFAULT 100 (placeholder, small for smoke runs; O39). Optimizer steps to run. |
| `train.hyperparams.batch_size` | int | 4 | DEFAULT | DEFAULT 4 (brief). Examples per forward pass. |
| `train.hyperparams.grad_accum_steps` | int | 4 | DEFAULT | DEFAULT 4 (placeholder; O39). Passes added up per optimizer step. |
| `train.hyperparams.warmup_steps` | int | 10 | DEFAULT | DEFAULT 10 (placeholder; O39). Linear warmup, then linear decay to 0. |
| `train.hyperparams.weight_decay` | float | 0.0 | DEFAULT | DEFAULT 0.0. AdamW weight decay. |
| `train.hyperparams.max_grad_norm` | float | 1.0 | DEFAULT | DEFAULT 1.0 (brief). Gradient clipping. |
| `train.hyperparams.seed` | int \| None | null | DEFAULT | DEFAULT none = use runtime.seed. Applied to Python, numpy, torch and the data order. |
| `train.log_every_steps` | int | 10 | DEFAULT | DEFAULT 10. A metrics record every N steps (and at step 1). |
| `train.eval_every_steps` | int | 50 | DEFAULT | DEFAULT 50. Val loss every N steps (and once at the end). |
| `train.save_every_steps` | int | 100 | DEFAULT | DEFAULT 100. A checkpoint every N steps (more are saved at a new best, a stop and the end). |
| `train.early_stopping.patience` | int | 5 | DEFAULT | DEFAULT 5 evaluations without improvement. |
| `train.early_stopping.min_delta` | float | 0.0 | DEFAULT | DEFAULT 0.0. An evaluation improves only if it is lower by more than this. |
| `train.max_runtime_minutes` | float \| None | null | DEFAULT | DEFAULT none = no cap. Per call: the run saves and stops gracefully. |
| `train.cpu_threads` | int \| None | null | DEFAULT | DEFAULT none = half of the cores (at least 1). |
| `train.resume` | bool | false | DEFAULT | DEFAULT false. true continues from the latest checkpoint of the output folder. |
| `train.save_optimizer_state` | bool | true | DEFAULT | DEFAULT true (the behaviour before this key existed). true: a checkpoint holds the model weights AND the optimizer, scheduler and random state, so the run can be resumed. false: a checkpoint holds only the model weights (about one third of the disk space, the Hugging Face option `save_only_model`), and the run CANNOT be resumed: `train.resume` true is refused with a clear message, in this mode and for any checkpoint made in it. |
| `train.rename_retries` | int | 5 | DEFAULT | DEFAULT 5. When the finished model folder cannot be renamed into place (on Windows another program, for example the antivirus, the search indexer or a sync tool, can hold the new folder for a moment: `PermissionError`, O122), the rename is tried again this many times after the first failure (0 = no retry). If every attempt fails, the `.tmp` folder with the finished model and the finished checkpoint are kept and the run fails with a message that says how to continue. |
| `train.rename_retry_seconds` | float | 2.0 | DEFAULT | DEFAULT 2.0. Seconds to wait before each new rename attempt (see `train.rename_retries`). |
| `train.output_dir` | Path \| None | null | DEFAULT | Per experiment, set by the RunManager. The caller copies it into TrainRequest.output_dir. |
| `train.sinks` | list[str] | ["csv", "console"] | DEFAULT | DEFAULT csv, console. Registered: csv, console. |

<a id="section-report"></a>
## `report`

The `report` section.

| Key | Type | Default | Status | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `report.title` | str \| None | null | DEFAULT | DEFAULT none = the experiment name. The title of the page. |
| `report.attributes` | list[str] | ["duration", "label_tokens", "ref_words", "extra_meta_quality_score", "flag_had_digits", "flag_had_latin", "flag_had_brackets"] | DEFAULT | DEFAULT duration, label_tokens, ref_words, extra_meta_quality_score (only if present), flag_had_digits, flag_had_latin, flag_had_brackets. The per-file attributes whose rank correlation with the per-file WER is shown. They are the keys the Orchestrator gives the Evaluator (`duration`, `ref_words`, `label_tokens`, `extra_<column>`, `flag_<text flag>`); the brief's names (duration_sec, meta_quality_score, had_digits ...) are the same things before that naming. A `flag_*` attribute that a file does not carry counts as 0. Open to change after the owner sees the first output. |
| `report.min_points_for_correlation` | int | 30 | DEFAULT | DEFAULT 30. Fewer points: the per-file correlation row says `too few points` and shows no number; the search correlation is shown with a caveat. |
| `report.max_points_per_chart` | int | 2000 | DEFAULT | DEFAULT 2000. More points in a scatter or a curve are thinned deterministically (every k-th) and the page says so. |
| `report.groups_shown` | int | 15 | NEW | NEW, DEFAULT 15. How many groups (lessons) the group table lists: the worst ones by the winner's WER. |
| `report.histogram_bins` | int | 20 | NEW | NEW, DEFAULT 20. Bins of the per-file WER histogram. |
| `report.loss_noise_range` | float | 0.01 | NEW | NEW, DEFAULT 0.01 (owner decision 2026-10-07). A Val-loss chart whose plotted values vary by less than this (in loss units) gets the note `Differences this small are noise`; the axis stays automatic. |
| `report.absolute_audio_paths` | bool | false | NEW | NEW, DEFAULT false (owner decision 2026-10-07). false: the listening list shows each audio path relative to the data folder (when the file is inside it); true: the full path as stored. |
| `report.target_relative_wer_reduction` | float \| None | null | NEW | NEW, DEFAULT none (owner decision 2026-10-07). The improvement target: a relative reduction of the Val WER against the baseline of the same Val set; 0.10 means 10% (baseline 0.60 -> 0.54 or lower). When set, the report and the summary of `run` say `reached` or `not reached`, and the history chart draws the target. none: the line only shows the reduction (`no target set`). |
| `report.hints.enabled_rules` | list[str] \| None | null | DEFAULT | DEFAULT none = every registered rule. Registered: overfitting, no_learning, unstable_training, gain_concentrated, short_clip_weakness, length_cap_or_empty, edge_of_range, failed_or_pruned. |
| `report.hints.overfitting_last_k_evals` | int | 3 | DEFAULT | DEFAULT 3. overfitting: the Val loss rose at each of the last K evaluations while the training loss fell over the same span. |
| `report.hints.no_learning_min_rel_improvement` | float | 0.01 | DEFAULT | DEFAULT 0.01. no_learning: the best Val loss is less than this share better than the first one. |
| `report.hints.unstable_spike_factor` | float | 2.0 | DEFAULT | DEFAULT 2.0. unstable_training: a training loss above this many times the median of the 5 records before it. |
| `report.hints.gain_top_group_fraction` | float | 0.1 | DEFAULT | DEFAULT 0.1. gain_concentrated: the best this share of the groups (lessons) ... |
| `report.hints.gain_share` | float | 0.5 | DEFAULT | DEFAULT 0.5. ... account for at least this share of the total word-error reduction. |
| `report.hints.short_clip_quantile` | float | 0.25 | DEFAULT | DEFAULT 0.25. short_clip_weakness: the shortest this share of the files ... |
| `report.hints.short_clip_wer_ratio` | float | 1.5 | DEFAULT | DEFAULT 1.5. ... has a WER at least this many times that of the other files. |
| `report.hints.length_cap_share` | float | 0.05 | DEFAULT | DEFAULT 0.05. length_cap_or_empty: at least this share of the files hit the length cap or are empty. |
| `report.hints.failed_share` | float | 0.3 | DEFAULT | DEFAULT 0.3. failed_or_pruned: at least this share of the started trials failed or were pruned. |
| `report.progress.refresh_seconds` | int | 10 | DEFAULT | DEFAULT 10. The page asks the browser to reload itself every this many seconds. |
| `report.progress.every_n_records` | int | 1 | DEFAULT | DEFAULT 1. The page is written again after every this many metrics records. |
